item.title: Ronaldinho returns to football with Italian third tier
item.description: Brazil legend Ronaldinho will make his playing return aged 46 next month for Ravenna, the third-division Italian club announced on Saturday. The 2002 World Cup winner’s move to Ravenna was announced in June. He is aiming to score his 300th career goal. The former Paris Saint-Germain, Barcelona and AC Milan playmaker retired in 2015, 10 years on from claiming the Ballon d’Or and has become a shareholder in Ravenna, situated between Venice and San Marino. “The wait now has a date: Sunday, November 15,” Ravenna said in a statement. “The Brazilian legend will wear the Ravenna FC shirt in the derby against Forli. “An event that will turn the eyes of the world toward the Bruno Benelli Stadium.” Ravenna are second in Group B of the Italian third tier, six points below leaders Spezia and are aiming for a return to Serie B for the first time since 2008. item.title: Southampton end West Ham’s unbeaten run, Burnley sack manager
item.description: Southampton ended West Ham’s nine-match unbeaten run with a 3-2 win at the London Stadium to surge into the Championship top six despite starting the season with a four-point deduction. Saints began the campaign with the points penalty after spying on opposition training sessions, which also cost them the chance of promotion in the play-off final last season. Kuryu Matsuki, James Bree and Lewis Dobbin all struck before half-time for the visitors, who are now within three points of the automatic promotion places. Kyle Walker-Peters and Tomas Soucek replied for the Hammers, but there were swathes of empty seats and boos by full-time as they missed the chance to go top. “This is a tough place to come, against a quality team, and we knew we needed to start strongly, so we worked on that all week,” said Saints boss Tonda Eckert after his side went 2-0 up inside the opening 10 minutes. “They made it tough for us in the second half, so it was important that we stayed brave to bring the result over the line.” Burnley sacked manager Nicky Hayen after just 14 games in charge following his side’s 4-1 defeat at Lincoln, which left the Clarets in the relegation zone. Relegated from the Premier League last season, former Club Brugge boss Hayen won just one of his 12 league matches in charge. “Burnley Football Club has dismissed head coach Nicky Hayen with immediate effect,” the club said in just a two-sentence statement. “The board has taken the decision following a disappointing start to the Championship season.” Swansea’s missed the chance to retake top spot after they were thrashed 5-0 by QPR at Loftus Road. Richard Kone scored a hat-trick inside the first 15 minutes before Jimmy Dunne’s double rounded off a remarkable scoreline that nudges Rangers into the play-off places. Adam Armstrong scored the only goal as fourth-placed Wolves beat struggling Watford 1-0 to move within two points of the automatic promotion places. Two people were “seriously” injured, Nunez said: one man in Toulouse, who reportedly had fingers blown off, and another person in Clermont-Ferrand. He did not give details of either case. Nunez said the confrontations lasted two hours and involved “500 rioters” at the back of the march. AFP journalists saw police charge several times and vigorously use tear gas and batons against some, mostly young, protesters. Protesters hold antifascist banners and flags as they face CRS riot police in a street by the Campo Santo Antifascist village set as part of a counter-mobilisation “against racism, fascism and imperialism” on the sidelines of the congress of the far-right party Rassemblement National (RN) in Orleans, central France, on October 24, 2026. In Lyon, police used tear gas to disperse around 1,000 people gathered in the south of the city. “If they prohibit protests then that means we are heading more and more towards a regime that is fascist, that is dictatorial,” said one 20-year-old protester in Lyon, who gave only his first name, Silem. In the southern cities of Cannes and Montpellier, far-right activists came out onto the streets seeking confrontations with “ultra-left militants”, in what authorities said was an unprecedented development. Meanwhile, the Yellow Vests, who staged disruptive protests against Macron eight years ago, called for more demonstrations on October 31 for “the freedom to protest”. Far-left presidential candidate Jean-Luc Melenchon, who marched in the Paris rally, said Macron “is going to understand that this is going to repeat itself every week”. Several protesters leaving after clashes in Paris taunted officers with a “see you next Saturday”. Protest against Le Pen’s party Tensions were heightened by a rally in the city of Orleans by far-right leader Marine Le Pen’s National Rally party to kick off her campaign for the presidential election. Thousands of counter-protesters chanting anti-fascist slogans marched in the city. Police put their number at 13,000 while organisers said twice as many participated. The unrest across France highlighted the febrile political atmosphere ahead of the vote, in which Le Pen leads in surveys. Inflation in France, particularly affecting the cost of fuel, has surged since the start of the Middle East war in February. Protests have also been taking place in Italy, Belgium, Spain and Portugal over different issues, yet with some overlap on inflation and education problems. item.title: Woman killed, two injured on Plateau farm
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa, Jos A woman has been killed, while two others sustained injuries while harvesting groundnuts on a farm at Gwom-Ajang, Foron District, in Barkin Ladi Local Government Area of Plateau State. The incident occurred at about 4pm on Saturday, according to a member of the community, Silas Bitrus, who confirmed the incident to our correspondent. Bitrus said, “The incident occurred around 4pm while they were harvesting groundnuts on the farm.” He added, “A woman was killed, while two others sustained injuries.” Also confirming the incident, the National Publicity Secretary of the Berom Youth Moulders, BYM, Rwang Tengwong, condemned the attacks and urged security operatives to go after the attackers. Also in a related development, the Coalition of Plateau State Indigenous Youth Bodies has alleged a plot by some groups to launch a counter-propaganda campaign against the Department of State Services, DSS, and other security agencies operating in the state. In a statement made available to newsmen on Saturday and signed by Amb. Ezekiel Peter Bini, Chairman, Coalition of Indigenous Youth Nationalities, Plateau State; Dalyop Solomon Mwantiri, President, Berom Youth Moulder-Association; Amb. Miri Timnan Nyantau, President, Tarok Progressive Youths Association; and Mr Jonathan Kyesmang Yusuf, President, Mwaghavul Youths Movement, the coalition said, “Following our World Press Conference held at the Nigerian Union of Journalists Secretariat in Abuja on 21st October, 2026, the Coalition has received information of a plan to launch an aggressive counter-propaganda campaign.” The group said, “According to reliable sources, some groups are planning to stage a World Press Conference to portray the joint operations of the Department of State Services (DSS), the Mobile Police Force, and Operation Rainbow as discriminatory against a section of the population.” The coalition further said, “The propaganda being launched must not be accepted as truth without independent verification.” “We challenge anyone concerned about human rights and freedom to demand evidence and allow the appropriate authorities to establish the facts.” The group added, “We stand firmly with the DSS, Mobile Police and Operation Rainbow and other security operatives.” “We will not be distracted by propaganda, nor shall we retreat because of terror. Plateau is our heritage and must remain safe for all law-abiding citizens.” The post Woman killed, two injured on Plateau farm appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: EPL: De Zerbi hails ‘complete’ Spurs after historic win at Chelsea
item.description: Roberto De Zerbi said Tottenham’s historic 2-0 victory against London rivals Chelsea proved his side have a winning mentality as they banished their dismal start to the season. Tottenham won at Stamford Bridge in the Premier League for just the second time in 36 years and the first since 2018. Trips across the capital to west London have largely been fruitless experiences for Tottenham over the last four decades. But De Zerbi’s men enjoyed a memorable visit to the Bridge on Saturday thanks to a comical own goal from Chelsea goalkeeper Mike Penders and a late wonder-goal from Mathys Tel after Blues star Cole Palmer was sent off. “It was a big moment for the fans, the club and the players also. They deserved this win, they prepared very well,” De Zerbi said. “We are improving a lot, we are improving in the mentality, in the group and the relationships with the players and then we are improving on the pitch.” Tottenham started the season on a dismal run of six league games without a win, raising the spectre of another relegation battle after they narrowly avoided dropping into the Championship on the final day of last season. With the pressure mounting on De Zerbi, the Italian has drawn his players closer together thanks to meals together and a trip to Marbella. – ‘The spirit, the belief’ – A win against promoted Coventry on Monday lifted the tension around the north London club and vanquishing Chelsea was another reward for De Zerbi’s team-building ethos. “Now it is a complete team. item.title: 2027: Northern power brokers, Emirs, Imams behind Tinubu, Yari assures
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: Director General of the All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council APC-PCC, Senator Abdul’aziz Yari, has assured President Bola Tinubu that the power brokers of Northern Nigeria, traditional rulers and Islamic clerics are solidly behind his return to office in 2027. He spoke at the flag-off of the party’s presidential campaign in Kaduna, in the presence of the President and all the governors of Northern Nigeria. “We have been engaging all and sundry, our traditional rulers, our ulama and our imams, to understand the importance of your return in 2027 for continuity, for the peace of this country and for Nigeria,” Yari said. He told the President that the northern establishment had turned out in full. “We believe in you, and those people believe in us. All the shakers and movers of this part of the country are here. In the northern part of the country, anybody who is not here today, Mr President, then there is nobody there. We are here. “By God’s grace, Your Excellency, Mr President, we resolve, by God’s grace, that as far as Northern Nigeria is concerned, Mr President, I need your ears. Mr President, I want you to listen to us carefully. Northern Nigeria is 101 per cent for you, Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Tinubu, by God’s grace, Insha Allah. item.title: ADC mocks APC over ‘rented crowds, empty seats’ at Kaduna rally
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council, ADC-PCC, has mocked the All Progressives Congress, APC, over what it described as a disappointing Northwest zonal flag-off rally in Kaduna, alleging that rented crowds and empty seats exposed the ruling party’s declining public acceptance. The council said the rally, which was intended to showcase the APC’s political strength across the Northwest, fell short of expectations despite alleged mobilisation of attendees from the seven states in the zone and beyond. In a statement by its Director of Media and Publicity, Kola Ologbondiyan, the ADC-PCC alleged that attendees were reportedly paid between ₦50,000 and ₦100,000 each, yet the Kaduna Township Stadium, which it put at a capacity of 5,000, remained sparsely occupied. “For a rally billed as the Northwest zonal flag-off, what we witnessed was a shameful spectacle. Despite the alleged mobilisation of crowds from across the zone and beyond, the stadium remained scantily filled, with empty seats everywhere,” Ologbondiyan said. He also faulted the reception given to speeches by APC leaders, describing it as unenthusiastic and at odds with the ruling party’s attempt to project political strength in the region. The ADC-PCC further questioned President Bola Tinubu’s performance claims, criticising his reported commissioning of road projects at the rally. Ologbondiyan alleged that some attendees expressed dissatisfaction with the APC after leaving the stadium, chanting “Ba mu yi,” a Hausa expression he interpreted as a rejection of the ruling party and its policies. “You can rent a crowd, but you cannot rent acceptance. Even if people attend a rally, that does not mean they have surrendered their convictions. The real test of public support is what Nigerians will decide at the ballot box,” he said. The council accused the APC of recycling promises made during the 2015, 2019 and 2023 election cycles without adequately accounting for its years in power. It also accused Tinubu of shifting responsibility for Nigerians’ economic hardship to opposition leaders instead of addressing the consequences of his administration’s policies, particularly fuel subsidy removal, which it said had intensified the pressure on households struggling with rising living costs. The ADC-PCC urged the ruling party to abandon what it called wasteful political jamborees, apologise to Nigerians over the prevailing economic difficulties and prepare for an orderly transfer of power in 2027. The council maintained that the ADC offered a credible alternative to the APC, expressing confidence that voters would use the next general election to reject the ruling party. “The message from Kaduna is loud and clear: Nigerians are saying ‘Ba mu yi’ to the APC and Tinubu. Come 2027, they will speak even louder with their votes,” Ologbondiyan declared. The post ADC mocks APC over ‘rented crowds, empty seats’ at Kaduna rally appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Nigeria-Indonesia investment to boost GDP, create jobs, says NICCI president, Balogun
item.description: By Favour Ulebor The President of the Nigerian Indonesian Chamber of Commerce and Industry, NICCI, Ishmael Balogun, has said increased investment between Nigeria and Indonesia, particularly in oil and gas exploration, will boost Nigeria’s Gross Domestic Product, GDP, create jobs and promote knowledge transfer. Balogun spoke during the Nigerian Indonesian Investment and Trade Forum, NIITF, which held its fifth edition in Jakarta from October 20 to 21, 2026, with a focus on expanding bilateral trade and investment in oil and gas, renewable energy, agriculture, pharmaceuticals and infrastructure development. He said stronger economic cooperation between the two countries would enable Nigerian businesses to access more opportunities in Indonesia while attracting foreign direct investment into Nigeria. item.description: By Anayo Okoli The African Democratic Congress (ADC) in Enugu State has called on the state government to ensure a level playing field for all political parties ahead of the 2027 general elections, alleging attacks on opposition supporters and urging authorities to prevent political violence. The party’s governorship candidate, Ocho Obodoeze, made the call after receiving an award from the Correspondents Chapel of the Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ), Enugu State Council. Obodoeze accused the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) of suppressing opposition parties and urged the state government to allow all political parties to campaign freely in accordance with the law. item.title: EPL: Arsenal see off Everton, go joint-top after Man City defeat
item.description: Manchester City’s flawless start to the Premier League season was ended in a 2-1 defeat at Aston Villa on Saturday that allowed Arsenal to join them at the top of the table with victory over Everton. Enzo Maresca had become the first manager to win his first seven Premier League games in charge of a new club but failed to find a solution to City’s struggles at Villa Park, where they have now lost for the past four seasons. Nicolas Jackson struck twice for Unai Emery’s men to continue a fine run of form for a new-look Villa side. Erling Haaland briefly levelled early in the second half, but Maresca was left to rue City not making more of their dominance for large spells of the game. “We lost because we probably are not being clinical enough in their box,” said Maresca. The Villa side that won the Europa League last season was decimated by high-profile departures during the transfer window. But Emery has quickly moulded his new squad into shape with Jackson proving his critics from a difficult spell at Chelsea wrong. The Senegal international pounced on an error by Marc Guehi to fire Villa ahead after just six minutes. Another of Villa’s new signings Zion Suzuki then thwarted City with a string of stunning saves. Haaland headed in his 13th goal in 10 games this season to equalise. Villa, though, swiftly responded as Gianluigi Donnarumma failed to keep out Jackson’s low shot on the hour mark. “A fantastic day to share with our supporters in Villa Park,” said Emery. “We felt that this is our fortress and the energy the supporters gave us was really fantastic.” – Arsenal’s set-piece prowess – Arsenal took advantage to move alongside City on 21 points from eight games with a routine 2-0 win against Everton. Shorn of the creative inspiration of Bukayo Saka, who is set for a lengthy spell on the sidelines with a thigh injury, Arsenal had to rely on their set-piece prowess to get the job done. Ezri Konsa bundled in his first goal for the club after Everton failed to clear a corner to open the scoring on seven minutes. Fellow centre-back Gabriel Magalhaes doubled the lead for Mikel Arteta’s men midway through the second period. Fulham further eased the pressure on manager Alvaro Arbeloa with a 1-0 win at Coventry thanks to Oscar Bobb’s individual effort. A second consecutive victory propels the Cottagers out of the relegation zone and up to 12th. Tottenham are also seeking to escape the bottom three when they travel to Chelsea in the evening kick-off, aiming to improve on a terrible record at Stamford Bridge. On Sunday the focus turns on Manchester United boss Michael Carrick when his side take on Bournemouth. A seven-game winless streak has plunged Carrick’s future into doubt just months after he was hired on a two-year deal after a successful interim spell in charge at the end of last season. Olaniyan identified the Constitution, Child Rights Act, Violence Against Persons legislation, National Health Act 2014, medical ethics rules, immigration laws and relevant data-protection provisions as instruments with implications for assisted reproduction. However, he said these laws largely provide general protections rather than detailed regulations covering IVF, intracytoplasmic sperm injection, gamete and embryo donation, fertility preservation and surrogacy. The lawyer stressed that informed consent, confidentiality, parental rights, children’s identities and the responsibilities of medical facilities required clear safeguards. He said properly drafted agreements and independent legal advice were important but could not replace comprehensive legislation. Olaniyan urged fertility practitioners to explain treatment options, risks and implications adequately, avoid promising outcomes that medical science could not guarantee, and ensure children conceived through assisted reproduction were not discriminated against because of their birth circumstances. Chairman of the House of Representatives Committee on Healthcare Services, Amos Gwamna Magaji, said the National Assembly was working towards addressing regulatory gaps in surrogacy and assisted reproductive procedures. Magaji disclosed that proposed legislation establishing a Nigerian Surrogacy Regulatory Commission had passed second reading in the House in October 2024, with further work required to strengthen the proposed framework. He said the legislation was intended to provide oversight for surrogacy arrangements and protect surrogate mothers, intended parents and children through provisions addressing informed consent, legal parentage, exploitation, medical supervision and accountability for fertility clinics. Acknowledging that religious and cultural objections had complicated previous attempts to regulate assisted reproduction, Magaji urged Nigerians to show greater understanding towards families struggling with infertility. He also advocated stronger health insurance coverage and sustainable financing to reduce treatment costs for low-income families. Founder of Circle Mom Fertility Foundation, Dr Charles Ojeabuo, said the organisation was established to ensure financial hardship did not permanently deny couples the opportunity to become parents. Ojeabuo said the foundation’s mission rested on three pillars: awareness, access and action. He disclosed that it had conducted 8,500 free fertility consultations and registrations during its first year while providing discounted treatment to families. The foundation, he said, was offering 10 free IVF slots, although more than 150 families had applied for assistance. “We will ensure that people will not have to choose between financial limitations and their dream of parenthood,” he said. Citing the World Health Organisation’s estimate that approximately one in six people worldwide experience infertility during their lifetime, Ojeabuo said many couples endure repeated treatment failures, mounting expenses and intense social pressure without adequate emotional or financial support. He disclosed that the foundation also runs a programme known as Mothers and Fathers of Faith, which provides emotional and spiritual encouragement to couples undergoing fertility treatment. He appealed to government agencies, employers, philanthropists and corporate organisations to support fertility care through funding, public education and patient-protection policies. Ojeabuo further advocated livelihood and empowerment support for women whose careers and financial stability were affected by prolonged fertility treatment, stressing the need for a more comprehensive support system for affected families.
